Brand
Guidelines

Logos drawn in SVG, and the whole kit around them.

Logowright is a Claude Code plugin that designs a logo as clean SVG from a short brief, sets the name in real typefaces so you choose by eye, and exports the whole brand kit around it from one file.

The mark is a drafting compass seen from its top: its arms and legs come down to two points and make a W, with the north star in front, for drawing and finding your way with one instrument.

Logo

01

Use the full logo wherever there is room, and the mark alone where space is small or square. On dark grounds use the dark version; where only one ink is available, use the one-colour logo in black or white.

Logo rules

02

Construction

On a 256 grid: arms 20 wide and legs, hinge ring and handle 10 wide (the one secondary weight), the legs fixed into the arms' feet; a four-point star of radius 40 on the centre line, set 6 clear of the compass. The dashed line is the clear space: 25 % of the mark’s height on every side, kept free of text and other graphics.

Minimum size

Below its minimum width, step down to the mark; below 32 px use the favicon.

One colour

Misuse

App and web icons

Files in icons/. Platforms round or mask the corners themselves; supply the square art as it is.

Logos drawn in SVG, and the whole kit around them.

Headings are set in Outfit at 600 with slightly tight spacing; body copy in Inter at 400, 16–18 px on screen and 10–12 pt in print, with a line height around 1.5. Keep lines to 60–75 characters. Both are free Google Fonts: load them from fonts.google.com or self-host the files.

Website colour

05

Every colour a website needs, made from the brand colours in OKLCH so steps of equal lightness look equal. Each scale has twelve steps, each with one job: 1–2 page and panel backgrounds, 3–5 component fills (rest, hover, pressed), 6–8 borders, 9–10 solid fills and their hover, 11–12 text. The brand colours themselves are kept exactly where they read.

Build with roles, not steps

Components use the named roles (--bg, --surface, --text, --text-muted, --brand with --on-brand, --border, --danger-subtle with --danger-text …). Each role has a light and a dark value, so dark mode follows the system on its own, or data-theme on the page forces either. Files in web/: palette.css, palette.tailwind.css for Tailwind v4, tokens.json (W3C Design Tokens) for Figma and Style Dictionary, and palette.html with every value.

Every pair in web/palette.html passes WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for edges). Lc is the APCA score from the WCAG 3 draft: 75 for body text, 60 for other text.
